title: Static application security testing, including F# coverage
status_rationale: The Secure Construction Standard proposes compiler semantic analysis to fill F# gaps and semantic checks for prohibited constructs; no SAST is configured in Echelon repositories reviewed, and the proposed owner (Aegis) is actually a fault-handling library, not a SAST orchestrator.
target_answer: Every merge runs available .NET analyzers, F# analyzers built on FSharp.Analyzers.SDK, and Echelon custom semantic rules that detect use or bypass of prohibited constructs (dynamic SQL outside Strata, dynamic code loading, unsafe interop, unrestricted deserialization, application JavaScript outside Limen); generated JavaScript bundles are scanned with a JavaScript-capable engine; coverage limits are stated per weakness class.
current_practice: Not established. No security static analysis workflow found. Dokimos measures code quality, not security.
intended_practice: Select and build F# analyzers, assign an owner (not Aegis), and integrate into Praxis gates.
customer_statement: Static security analysis for Unbound is planned, including custom F# rules, because mainstream SAST tools do not analyze F#. It is not yet operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Which system will own the security rule registry, given that Aegis is not a SAST orchestrator?

challenge.customer_intent: Confidence that common coding weaknesses are caught before release.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Injection, deserialization or similar flaws reach production.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Commercial and open-source SAST tools largely do not support F#; running a C#-oriented tool over an F# codebase produces a clean report that proves nothing. Academic evaluations show substantial false negative rates even in supported languages.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly asked as yes or no; rarely specified by tool.
challenge.historical_convention: Questionnaires ask whether SAST runs and which tool.
challenge.architectural_elimination: SEC-DB-001 (no dynamic SQL, typed access), SEC-EXEC-001 and SEC-DATA-001 aim to make the dangerous sinks unavailable, so the weakness classes SAST hunts become structurally absent within scope, if bypass is independently verified.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Compiler warnings as errors, private constructors, restricted interfaces, and custom analyzers that detect bypass of approved interfaces.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Per-release evidence that prohibited APIs are absent and bypass tests pass.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Structural elimination plus bypass-detecting custom F# rules, validated against fixtures, instead of relying on generic SAST coverage claims.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, if fixtures, rules and bypass tests are published and reproducible.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain: customers recognize brand-name SAST tools; a structural argument requires explanation and independent confirmation.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Strata typed query interface not available (current-state brief says no verified runtime typed query interface); trusted infrastructure code outside rules; native interop.
challenge.alternative_risks: Custom analyzers maintained by a small team may lag; claims of elimination could be overstated, which the Standard itself warns against.
supporting_arguments: The Standard requires scoped evidence before claiming elimination.
Structural prevention fails closed; detection fails open.
opposing_arguments: Auditors and questionnaires expect a named SAST tool.
Structural guarantees depend on Strata capabilities not yet verified.

title: Software composition analysis
status_rationale: SEC-SUPPLY-001 proposes locked versions, provenance, SBOM, vulnerability and license checks; not implemented.
target_answer: Every build generates an SBOM and runs SCA against OSV and GitHub advisory data for NuGet and npm, including transitive dependencies, with license policy; deployed SBOMs are rescanned daily so new advisories against released artifacts are detected.
customer_statement: Dependency scanning is planned under Echelon's proposed supply-chain rule; not yet operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Secret scanning and response
status_rationale: SEC-CRYPTO-001 proposes secret scanning and rotation; SOC2-003 prohibits secrets in logs; neither is implemented.
target_answer: Pre-commit and push-time scanning blocks secrets; scheduled scans cover full history, CI logs, container images and persisted AI agent transcripts; any detected secret is treated as compromised, rotated and revoked, and its use investigated; scanning applies to all Echelon repositories.
current_practice: Unknown; no secret scanning configuration was located in reviewed repositories.
intended_practice: Enable push-time blocking and history scans across Echelon repositories.
customer_statement: Secret scanning is planned under Echelon's proposed cryptography rule; not yet verified as operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Dynamic testing (DAST, API testing, IAST, ASV)
status_rationale: No dynamic testing is defined in Echelon sources beyond the Standard's general reference to DAST reuse; PCI DSS is not expected to apply because Unbound is not known to process card data.
target_answer: Each release candidate deployed to a test cell is scanned with authenticated DAST and schema-driven API tests across all roles, including cross-tenant object access attempts; Limen boundary messages and other serialized inputs are fuzzed. IAST is not used unless a tool demonstrably supports F# on .NET. ASV scans are performed only if PCI DSS scope is ever introduced.
intended_practice: Implement once a deployable test environment exists.
customer_statement: Dynamic security testing is planned; not yet operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)
open_questions: Will Unbound ever accept card payments (which would bring PCI DSS and ASV scanning into scope)?

challenge.customer_intent: Confidence that the running application resists common attacks.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Generic DAST finds configuration and reflected-input issues but is weak at authorization and business-logic flaws; IAST support for F# on .NET is uncertain.
challenge.legally_required: No; PCI ASV external scans apply only where PCI DSS applies.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Server-side deny-by-default authorization (SEC-AUTH-001) and validated typed inputs reduce DAST yield.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Schema-driven negative authorization tests in CI.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Schema-driven negative authorization tests and boundary fuzzing as primary dynamic testing, with generic DAST as a supplement; skip IAST unless a tool demonstrably supports the stack.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, via test results tied to release hashes.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely if DAST is still run.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Missing API schemas or incomplete role models.
challenge.alternative_risks: Tests only cover the authorization model as specified, not as misunderstood.
supporting_arguments: Broken object level authorization is the top API risk and is best tested with knowledge of the object model.
opposing_arguments: Questionnaires may score absence of IAST negatively.

title: Infrastructure-as-code, container, configuration and schema scanning
status_rationale: Hosting and IaC are not selected; Strata provides schema diff (pilot, PG16) but no security rules.
target_answer: IaC, container images and Strata schema diffs are scanned before deployment; deployed cloud configuration is continuously compared to the approved baseline (CIS Benchmarks) and drift outside the pipeline raises an alert.
intended_practice: Implement once hosting and IaC are selected.
customer_statement: Infrastructure and configuration scanning is planned; Unbound has no deployed infrastructure.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Scanner validation and false negative measurement
status_rationale: The Secure Construction Standard specifies benchmarking with NIST SAMATE, SARD and SATE and OWASP Benchmark, F#-specific fixtures, holdout cases and publication of methodology; nothing has been built.
target_answer: Each scanner and rule set release is validated against public suites where applicable and Echelon F# vulnerable and safe fixtures with independently constructed holdouts; precision, recall, false positive and false negative rates are reported by weakness class; recall regressions block adoption; vulnerabilities that escaped scanners become new fixtures; methodology, fixtures and limitations are published, and benchmarking is never represented as accreditation.
intended_practice: Build the fixture corpus and validation harness as part of the scanner program.
customer_statement: Echelon plans to measure and publish scanner detection rates, including false negatives, for its F# stack; no results exist yet.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

challenge.customer_intent: Know whether scanner output can be trusted.
challenge.adverse_outcome: False assurance from scanners that miss whole classes of weaknesses.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Most vendors never measure scanner false negative rates; a clean report is treated as evidence of absence.
challenge.historical_convention: Tool selection by reputation, not measurement.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Validation suite runs on every scanner or rule update.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Versioned validation reports with precision and recall by weakness class.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Published, reproducible scanner validation with F# fixtures and holdouts, as the Standard proposes.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, if fixtures and methodology are published.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely as a differentiator; may be ignored by checklist reviewers.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Fixtures written by the same people or agents who write rules (overfitting); benchmark suites not representative of F#.
challenge.alternative_risks: Published fixtures could help attackers understand gaps; publish methodology and limitations while withholding exploitable specifics.
supporting_arguments: Measurement converts a tool claim into evidence.
opposing_arguments: Cost and effort for a small team before any customer asks for it.

title: Scan frequency, coverage, gating and suppression governance
status_rationale: The Standard requires fail-closed merge and release gates on mandatory rule failures or missing evidence; CNV-PLT-010 requires two approvers on control-relevant modules and signed builds; none is implemented.
target_answer: SAST, SCA and secret scans run on every merge; DAST and IaC scans on every release candidate; deployed artifacts rescanned daily; scan evidence older than the release commit blocks release. Gates fail closed on missing evidence. Scanner configuration lives outside the repository under change control. Suppressions need a non-author human approver, expire and are re-reviewed; AI agents cannot alter scanner configuration, gates or suppressions. Coverage is reported against the full inventory.
current_practice: Not established. Praxis CI workflows exist for repository governance but contain no security scanning step.
intended_practice: Add scanning gates to Praxis-managed CI.
customer_statement: Fail-closed security gates are planned; not yet operating.
owner: Unassigned (proposed role: Security Lead, per UNB-CTRL matrix proposed owners)

title: Sharing scan results with customers
status_rationale: The Standard lists a continuous security assurance summary monthly and labeling of first-party reports; none produced.
target_answer: Customers receive a signed, release-specific scan summary (counts by severity and scanner, open critical findings, coverage, gate outcome) labeled as first-party evidence, plus a monthly assurance summary; raw SARIF is available under NDA on request.
intended_practice: Generate from the evidence bundle once scanning operates.
customer_statement: Scan summaries are planned; none exist because scanning is not yet operating.
